images.title: A value above the median moves it up
images.purpose: Shows that including 11, which is above the median 8, makes the two middle values 8 and 11 and the median 9.5.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Two rows of number boxes, one above the other: the sorted data before on top and after below, with the middle marked in each.
images.exact_structure: Top row: 5 equal square boxes in a line holding 3, 5, 8, 12, 14 in that order; the middle box 8 has a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline and the label median 8 under it; the other boxes have thin dark outlines. Bottom row, centred under the top row: 6 equal boxes holding 3, 5, 8, 11, 12, 14; the box 11 is filled light amber (#E69F00) to show it is new, and a thin amber arrow comes down into it from above. The two middle boxes 8 and 11 share one reddish purple bracket under them with the label median 9.5. No other marks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A new value above the median pushes the middle up: (8 + 11) ÷ 2 = 9.5.
images.description: Shows that including 11, which is above the median 8, makes the two middle values 8 and 11 and the median 9.5.
images.context: Values other than 8 and 11 are an illustrative sorted set with median 8; the new median (8 + 11) / 2 = 9.5 matches the concept.
images.teaching_notes: Point at the number of boxes left and right of the middle before and after.

image_decisions.why: A sorted row before and after a new value makes the moving middle easy to see.
